spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: A family is presented as an analytic technology for deforming and averaging objects that are inaccessible one at a time. The sharp distinction is between universal high-zero behavior and low-zero behavior that retains the family's arithmetic formation.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source proposes working definitions of number-field families as parametrized subsets of automorphic representations, motivated by density theorems, subconvexity through deformation, and function-field geometric families. It says trace formulas, monodromy, and geometry of numbers can isolate and average these sets, while high scaled zero spacings are already expected to follow universal GUE statistics.
directed.conceptual_reading: Formation is part of the mathematical object: it supplies an ordering, an averaging mechanism, and local data. Low-zero statistics can therefore depend on how the L-functions vary even when high-zero spacings forget that structure.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is the parameter map into A(GLn), which converts a collection of completed L-functions into an analyzable statistical ensemble.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The opening offers a working scope, not a formal exhaustive definition, and explicitly admits that number-field families lack a canonical general notion.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The source supplies two family factories with different parameter spaces but the same output interface. Harmonic families isolate spectra and push them through an L-group representation; geometric families specialize cohomology and, conditionally on modularity, convert it to automorphic data.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: A harmonic family is a trace-formula-isolable set H⊂A(H) with a dual-group representation r giving r*:H→A(GLn). A geometric family starts from a smooth proper X→W, restricts rational parameters to a cone, takes fixed-degree étale cohomology, and uses modularity plus a |det|^{d/2} twist to obtain unitary-normalized automorphic representations. Products are allowed; intersections can introduce uncontrolled Diophantine equations.
directed.conceptual_reading: The definition separates parameter formation from the automorphic image. That separation records multiplicity and ordering and explains why two constructions can yield comparable L-function families without sharing an ontology.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The L-group map r and the cohomology-to-automorphic modularity map are the two bridges; the unitarizing twist aligns their local normalization.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Functoriality and geometric modularity are often conjectural. Boolean intersections are not generally closed within the analyzable class, and conductor may be replaced only by a controlled gauge.
directed.uncertainty: Exact cohomological twists and dual-group notation should be scan-checked.

supported: The two constructions, parameter maps, trace-formula isolation, smooth proper specialization, cohomology, modularity, unitarizing twist, gauges, products, and intersection hazard are all explicit.
inference: Separating parameter formation from automorphic image and tracking multiplicity/order is a useful interpretation grounded in F=(W,F).
unsupported_or_imported: The phrase without sharing an ontology is project-style abstraction with no mathematical content supplied by the source.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: Most of the response is specific, but ontology language is a recognizable teacher template that could be pasted into unrelated comparisons.
context_or_ocr_risk: Dual-group notation, cohomological degree, determinant twist, and discriminant gauge require exact preservation.
missed_mechanism: The source emphasizes that the gauge only approximates conductor and that intersections can introduce global Diophantine equations; these are concrete formation constraints.
revision_instructions: Delete ontology language and replace it with the precise claim that both constructions yield maps into A(GL_n) while retaining different parameter-counting measures and hypotheses.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: For harmonic families, the L-group representation already contains the coarse invariants: irreducibility gives cuspidality, self-duality and Frobenius–Schur sign give type, and the next Plancherel coefficient forces rank zero. Partial L-functions make the low-zero formulation robust to uncertain ramified factors.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Macdonald's Plancherel formula yields a Sato–Tate measure from the image of the dual group. For irreducible r, i1=1; i2 records whether r is self-dual and i3 is its Frobenius–Schur indicator. The estimate tF(p)=O(p^{-1}) makes r(F)=0. Under a Ramanujan bound, nontrivial zeros of the partial L-function cannot be canceled by omitted local factors, and quantitative equidistribution proves restricted-support density results.
directed.conceptual_reading: Representation theory predicts type before full functorial transfer is constructed. Omitting ramified factors is a robustness move: it forgets delicate local data while preserving zeros in the relevant strip under the stated bounds.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The dual-group representation r and Macdonald measure bridge harmonic formation to the indicators; the partial L-function bridges available analytic continuation to low-zero tests.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Cuspidality of most functorial lifts may need a separate proof, root-number splitting remains subtle, and analytic continuation/Ramanujan inputs are not known uniformly.
directed.uncertainty: Exact pole-free regions and support ranges depend on formula-level hypotheses.

supported: Macdonald's measure, the indicator rules for irreducible r, t_F(p)=O(p^-1), rank zero, partial-factor robustness, restricted support dependence, and finite local constraints are explicit.
inference: Representation theory predicting homogeneity before full functorial transfer and partial L-functions isolating uncertain ramified factors are reasonable conceptual readings.
unsupported_or_imported: The spontaneous reading says irreducibility gives cuspidality without qualification; the source says i1=1 makes the family essentially cuspidal but explicitly warns that cuspidality of most functorial lifts needs a separate proof.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The robustness discussion is specific, but collapsing essentially cuspidal statistical behavior into actual cuspidality creates an overly polished false equivalence.
context_or_ocr_risk: Local pole-free regions, theta bounds toward Ramanujan, and restricted supports are formula-dependent.
missed_mechanism: Root-number splitting remains an additional invariant even after irreducibility, self-duality, and rank are computed.
revision_instructions: Change irreducibility gives cuspidality to irreducibility gives i1=1 and predicts/defines essential cuspidality; retain the source's separate-proof requirement for actual lifts.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Tensor products compose symmetry through multiplication of Frobenius–Schur indicators. This explains families whose fixed functional-equation sign would suggest the wrong random-matrix law and shows that root sign is not the fundamental classifier.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The family π×sym²(f) on GL6 is self-dual symplectic with root number +1 and has restricted-support SOeven statistics. More generally, for homogeneous families F1,F2, the predicted indicator satisfies i3(F1×F2)=i3(F1)i3(F2). Adjoint representations preserve the symmetric Killing form, so generic adjoint families are orthogonal and predicted to have Sp(∞) zero symmetry.
directed.conceptual_reading: The tensor product acts on bilinear pairings multiplicatively. The low-zero class follows this representation operation, whereas functional-equation parity supplies only a secondary refinement within symplectic families.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The tensor embedding and the identity tr(θ1⊗θ2)=tr(θ1)tr(θ2) bridge product measures to multiplied indicators.

unit_result_entry.why_material: The appendix defines conductor and local L-factor from inertia and monodromy, assembles them for algebraic l-adic representations, and formulates geometry as a cohomological source, providing the exact interface used by geometric families.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: Includes archimedean completion and the nonabelian reciprocity interpretation.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Extremely formula-dependent; conductors, invariants, twists, and Frobenius conventions require scan verification.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Automorphic induction combines varying fields with harmonic data beyond the basic formation
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The construction varies number fields, applies an L-group representation over each, and induces back to the rationals, showing how geometric and spectral parameters can be composed while common L-factors and mixed Galois types require explicit handling.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Modularity matches geometric Galois data to automorphic data and the weight twist restores unitarity
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The two conjectural formulations distinguish existence of an automorphic realization from a bijective algebraic correspondence with local-global compatibility; Deligne weights explain the precise twist making good-reduction local components unitary and identify weight-monodromy as the bad-reduction gate.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Weil–Deligne representations are the local interface that makes geometric and automorphic L-functions comparable even at ramified primes. Inertia invariants and monodromy jointly specify what the local factor preserves and what ramification removes.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: A Weil–Deligne object (V,ρ,N) has conductor defined from inertia and its filtration, and local factor det(1−Frob_K q_K^{-s}|V^{I_K}∩ker N)^{-1}. Local Langlands preserves these factors, epsilon factors, and conductors. An algebraic l-adic Galois representation gives such an object at every finite place, hence a global Euler product and an archimedean completion; étale cohomology supplies geometric examples.
directed.conceptual_reading: The local factor deliberately forgets ramified directions not fixed by inertia or killed by monodromy while retaining Frobenius on the stable quotient. That common representation is what allows local-global comparison across languages.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The functor WD_v followed by local reciprocity rec_K is the bridge between Galois cohomology and smooth GLn representations.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The Euler product initially converges only in a right half-plane; analytic continuation and automorphy are separate conjectural burdens. Definitions at l-adic places use deeper p-adic Hodge theory.
directed.uncertainty: Conductors, twists, Frobenius convention, and invariant subspaces are extremely notation-sensitive and should be checked against the PDF.

supported: The Weil-Deligne triple, conductor, local L-factor on V^{I_K} intersect ker N, local Langlands preservation, algebraic l-adic localizations, Euler product, completion, and geometric cohomology source are explicit.
inference: The local factor as a common interface explaining what ramification removes is a useful conceptual reading.
unsupported_or_imported: The pass calls V^{I_K} intersect ker N a stable quotient, but it is a subspace. It also says WD_v followed by rec_K, whereas the Galois-to-automorphic direction uses iota WD_v followed by rec_K^{-1}.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The interface language is substantive, but incorrect subspace/quotient and map-direction terminology would teach a polished false representation.
context_or_ocr_risk: Conductor filtration, Frobenius convention, invariant subspace, twists, and archimedean factors are extremely formula-sensitive.
missed_mechanism: The intersection simultaneously imposes inertia invariance and N-kernel; it is not obtained by quotienting ramified directions in the L-factor definition.
revision_instructions: Replace stable quotient with invariant subspace V^{I_K}∩ker N and write the automorphic bridge as rec_K^{-1}(iota WD_v(rho_v)); keep analytic continuation and automorphy as separate burdens.
